C0.quote: we consider two fundamental social choice problems: single-winner voting and one-sided matching
C0.note: Distortion of single-winner voting mechanisms (and one-sided matching) with predictions. Voting is a main object, so coded eligible.

C1.quote: we design mechanisms that achieve tight tradeoffs between consistency and robustness
C1.note: Distortion, consistency and robustness bounds with matching lower bounds. Mechanisms are simple and computation is not the focus, so AL is only a minor secondary type.

C2.1.value: ordinal preferences / ordinal profile (rankings reported by voters)
C2.1.quote: each voter i reports an ordering (or, ranking) ≻vi of the candidates

C2.2.quote: each voter i reports an ordering (or, ranking) ≻vi of the candidates
C2.2.note: The predicted valuation profile is an additional input (CARD) to the mechanism, but the voters' input is the ranking. Rankings are induced weakly (x ≻ y implies vi(x) ≥ vi(y)).

C2.3.quote: Each voter i ∈ N has a valuation function vi : A → R≥0

C2.4.quote: ordinal preferences of the voters which are induced by their valuation functions
C2.4.note: Valuations (v) and the ordinal profile (≻v) have separate notation. Rankings are induced by the valuations, though that is a consistency requirement rather than a sincerity claim.

C3.1.note: No analysis has voters misreporting strategically. Distortion is worst-case over valuations given the induced ordinal profile.

C3.2.quote: each voter i reports an ordering (or, ranking) ≻vi of the candidates
C3.2.note: Rankings are defined as induced by the valuations, so submission equals the held ranking. This is stated as part of the definition, with no reason given.

C3.3.note: No reason is given for the equality of reported and induced rankings.

C4.1.note: Rankings are consistent with unit-sum valuations.

C4.2.note: The term dichotomous preferences is not used.

C5.1.quote: The social welfare of a candidate x ∈ A is defined as the total value
C5.1.note: Distortion and social welfare are the evaluation criteria.

C5.2.note: Distortion is evaluated against the cardinal valuations v, which are defined separately from the ordinal input.

VOT.note: Voters supply induced rankings and take no strategic actions. By the C6 definition, an agent who takes a fixed action in the model could count as present, but the rankings are mechanically induced by the valuations and the analysis is worst-case over valuations.

C7.1.note: Fewer than two types are present.

claims.quote: aggregate the preferences of individuals into a collective outcome which is aligned with the well-being
improved distortion guarantees can be achieved when the prediction is accurate

C9.1.note: Claims are mostly about mechanism performance with respect to welfare, plus the interpretation of elicited cardinal values as predictions.

C9.2.quote: ordinal preferences of the voters which are induced by their valuation functions
C9.2.note: Welfare claims need the relation between rankings and values, and it is stated (rankings induced by valuations). The strategic issue does not arise since no strategic behaviour is modelled.

C10.1.note: The paper does not state a procedural reading.
